items.title: ❗️In Romania on the morning of 24 September, classes were temporarily suspended in schools in four localities of Suceava County (Solca, Arbore, Botoșana and Cacica) after a drone that entered from Ukraine violated the country’s airspace. The small UAV remained in Romanian airspace for about four minutes and crashed in a forest near Solca close to the border; there were no casualties or damage. Two Romanian F-16s and two Spanish F-18s stationed in the country as part of a NATO mission were scrambled to monitor the situation.

According to El Mundo, the aircraft — including Gerbera-type drones with a declared range of up to 600 km — could be delivered in ordinary shipping containers and launched directly from the vessel. This approach would expand Russia’s ability to strike military sites, airfields, and energy infrastructure without approaching Russian territory. The newspaper reports that the governments of Spain, France, and Italy have received a CIA warning about the risk of such attacks, including in the context of elections scheduled for 2027.

items.title: “When Russia started this war, it never imagined Ukrainian long-range drones would one day reach its military factories somewhere in Siberia,” President Zelensky told the UN General Assembly. Zelensky warned that if Russia continues striking Ukraine’s energy and heating systems, Ukraine will respond this winter. Separately, Zelensky warned that weapons technology is developing so rapidly that as early as next year there is a real possibility that AI, rather than only humans, could begin deciding what happens on the battlefield. #Ukraine

items.title: Russia lost 248,964 troops on the battlefield in Ukraine from January through August, President Zelensky says. He said Ukraine has video evidence documenting each Russian loss and an archive of drone footage showing thousands of Russian troops being killed in combat zones. Zelensky added Russia seized just over 1,000 km² of Ukrainian territory this year and that Ukraine has already liberated much of it. He also said Russia has launched more than 2,000 missiles of various types and 63,000 attack drones against Ukraine since the beginning of the year. Separately, Zelensky announced that Ukraine has successfully tested four new drone interceptors but warned that the coming winter could be very difficult.

items.title: RT by @RALee85: Hello everyone. Today I’m starting another fundraiser to get engineering equipment to Ukraine, and I’m asking for your help by sharing, donating, and liking this post. Even if you can’t donate, sharing it genuinely makes a difference. Plase watch the video with their CV90 Crew explaining the importance of this equipment. The donation link is in the comments below. A good friend of mine from the 21st Mechanized Brigade of the UAF has been working on improving the survivability and effectiveness of the 🇸🇪 CV90 IFVs and, most importantly, the soldiers inside them. He recently reached out to me asking for help getting engineering equipment for his brigade. This is one of those things that doesn’t look as dramatic as drones, armored vehicles, or weapons, but it directly saves lives. A properly dug fighting position, trench, vehicle shelter, or reinforced position can be the difference between soldiers surviving an artillery or drone attack and not coming home. Unfortunately, because of bureaucracy and often simple neglect by higher command, excavation equipment remains critically overlooked. It is one of the most obvious low-hanging fruits on the battlefield: relatively inexpensive machinery that can save soldiers’ lives and protect multimillion-dollar equipment. The brigade already has several excavators, but they are in critically bad condition. We are already working on getting those repaired. But even if every one of them were operational, it still wouldn’t be enough for the brigade’s needs. Their full request is for 3 excavators, transportation for them, a crane, and pickup trucks. The total cost would be around $240,000. I wish I could say we can raise all of it, but with the current level of donations, I don’t think that is realistic. So we scaled the fundraiser down to $100,000. That will allow us to purchase 3 excavators and a truck capable of transporting them. It is still a huge amount of money. But these machines will not sit somewhere in storage. They will be working every day, digging positions, protecting vehicles, and giving Ukrainian soldiers a better chance of surviving. And that is why I’m asking for your help. If you can donate, even a small amount helps. If you can’t donate, please like and repost this post. The more people who see it, the better chance we have of reaching this goal. Thank you to everyone who has supported our previous fundraisers and continues supporting Ukraine. Don't mind the snow in the video, they asked for this in march, and unfortunately I couldn't fundraiser until today. But we have been working on repairing their equipment and supplying some machines since June. Donation link is in the 1st comment below.

items.title: This never get old, every day Russia burns, I feel safer. Thank you Ukraine.

Thank you Ukraine.
Volodymyr Zelenskyy / Володимир Зеленський (@ZelenskyyUa)
Our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night. One of Russia’s key oil industry facilities and the aggressor’s logistics facility were hit. These are billions of dollars that sustain the war machine. The systems used included FP-1, RZ-100, MICH-2000, Palianytsia, Vendetta, Liutyi, Bars, Flamingo, Sichen, and Pelican.
I thank our warriors for their accuracy: the Security Service of Ukraine together with the Unmanned Systems Forces, the Special Operations Forces, the Defense Intelligence of Ukraine, and the Foreign Intelligence Service. Sanctions were also imposed on a facility in the Voronezh region. Moscow must end its brutal war and choose peace instead of building layered rings of air defense at the expense of other regions. Steps toward de-escalation are on the table – in energy and food security. What is needed is political will. I thank everyone who is strengthening Ukraine’s long-range capabilities. I am grateful to everyone who complements our long-range responses with responses through sanctions. Glory to Ukraine!
